messages:
ajay: heads up 999after the kernel-selector v3.4 rollout last night i'm seeing a new p99 regression on continuous-batching for long-context sessions (>=16k). symptoms: mid-token page faults on KV pages and eviction during merges, which causes HOL blocking. flamegraph attached: https://perf.internal/fg/1830001200
sarah: can you paste repro steps + env? :thinking:
dave: reproducer: `./tools/run_local --mode=hosted --profile=cont-batch --ctx=18k --clients=64` 999repro is stable. trace shows sequence: batch-merge -> kv_shard mutex wait -> vm_fault -> evict_range -> head stall. sampling shows a single shard owning most of the time in evict_range.
ajay: exactly. async-profile and perf show `kv_shard::evict_range` holding the shard lock for ~20-40ms during merge storms. that blocks the leading request and makes cont-batcher queue pile up.
elena: curious if this is classic fragmentation (tiny free/list churn) or working-set thrash (large slot reclamation). what do the allocator histograms say?
dave: allocator histos show alternating big frees and new allocations; also `kv_page_reclaim` events spike when concurrent cont-batches >50. RSS climbs across long sequences and then we see reclaim spikes during merge windows.
ajay: my working hypothesis: cont-batch merge causes many concurrent KV writes for overlapping prefixes. kernel-selector v3.4 changed packing so writes became sparser across pages, increasing fragmentation and VM faults. merging amplifies contention because many requests hit same shard simultaneously.
sarah: low-friction experiments we can run: (A) disable cont-batch merging entirely; (B) try compact allocator mode; (C) rollback kernel-selector. which to try first?
elena: flip `continuous_batch.merge_threshold=0` first (least risky). also try `kv.allocator=compact` on a canary.
dave: ran both on small canary pools. results: merge_threshold=0 reduced p99 from ~340ms to ~185-200ms. compact allocator lowered median RSS ~10-15% but p99 unaffected. so merge behavior is the dominant factor.
perf-bot: PERF ALERT 1830001280 — cont-batch KV eviction hotspot. top stacks: kv_shard::evict_range -> kv_page_reclaim -> handle_page_fault. related deploy: kernel-selector v3.4 (roll 1829999000).
ajay: proposed mitigations: 1) short-term: disable merging for hosted shared pools to reduce HOL stalls; 2) add granular metrics: `kv_shard.lock_wait_ms`, `kv_shard.evict_ops`, `kv_reclaim_time` to console; 3) medium-term: implement async reclaim (offload heavy eviction work to background thread so shard mutex isn't held across blocking vm_fault paths).
elena: async reclaim will need careful correctness checks (mark pages RECLAIMING, maintain invariants). i'll sketch a patch that marks pages and schedules background reclaim while briefly holding lock. add unit+integration tests to assert no double-free and correct read-after-reclaim behavior.
dave: additional note: this only reproduces on hosted shared GPUs, not on dedicated instances. suspect NUMA and kernel IO behavior plus allocator diffs in our shared images. might be interaction between userspace allocator and kernel page reclaim heuristics.
sarah: canary rollback results: rollback to selector v3.3 + merge_threshold=20 -> p99 ~330ms. rollback + merge_threshold=0 -> p99 ~175-190ms. disabling merges shows big wins but not a permanent solution.
ajay: i've filed infra/eng-runtime#4587 with reproducer, perf captures, and recommended mitigations. next steps: short-term disable merging on hosted; mid-term land async reclaim + allocator improvements; long-term revisit kernel-selector packing heuristics and continuous-batcher write coalescing to avoid scatterness. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility. :thumbsup:
